sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A rhizomatous perennial reaching up to about 2.5 m. Its deeply lobed leaves are dark green above and whitish or grey beneath; small creamy-yellow flower heads form leafy panicles. Native to temperate Eurasia, North Africa and Indochina, it has been introduced elsewhere.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The bitter leaves are eaten or used to flavour foods and drinks. Kew also records toxic uses for the species without specifying doses or plant parts; no general claim about human toxicity is made here.

sections.title: Related wormwoods
sections.text: Unlike the more uniformly silvery Artemisia absinthium, A. vulgaris has green upper leaf surfaces and pale undersides. A. maritima is a lower-growing relative associated with salt-marsh habitats.
